office_does: A State Senator writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, and the Senate confirms the governor's appointments.
race_blurb: Democratic incumbent Marko Liias, in the Senate since 2014 and chair of its Transportation Committee, faces Republican Riaz Khan, a former Mukilteo councilmember. Liias has voted for the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and other progressive tax bills; Khan campaigns on lower taxes, spending restraint and parental rights.

candidates.summary: Incumbent State Senator since 2014 and chair of the Senate Transportation Committee, a former state representative and Mukilteo councilmember whose record includes clean-fuels laws, progressive tax votes and student cellphone limits.
highlights: Chairs Senate Transportation; in the Legislature since 2008 [S1]
Voted for ESSB 6346, the 9.9% tax on income over $1 million, and ESSB 5813's capital gains and estate tax changes [S5][S7]
Lists clean fuels, building-emissions and greenhouse-gas tracking laws among his achievements [S3]
Prime sponsor of SB 5346, restricting student cellphone use in public schools [S11]
Voted for ESHB 1296 (2025), which amended the I-2081 parental-rights list [S6]

taxes.basis: Recorded votes for ESSB 6346 (tax on income over $1 million) and ESSB 5813 (more progressive capital gains and estate taxes), two independent tax votes.

spending.basis: Campaigns on transportation infrastructure jobs and lists school-funding and transportation packages as achievements; no stated restraint agenda.

housing.basis: Cites winning resources for affordable units and voted for EHB 1217 rent and fee limits, alongside calls for more housing near transit.

climate.basis: Lists the Low Carbon Fuel Standard, building-emissions standards and GHG tracking as achievements and voted for the 2025 clean fuels bill.

experience.basis: Senator since 2014, representative 2008-2014, current committee chair and former Majority Floor Leader.

local-control.basis: Says he has demanded more housing near light rail and voted for ESHB 2266's state rules on siting supportive housing and shelters.

tech.basis: Sponsored student cellphone restrictions and says he is working to tax large social media platforms and search engines to fund local news.

immigration.basis: Pamphlet cites advocacy for immigrant neighbors and protecting families from 'dangerous federal policies'; no specific bill cited.

social.basis: Pamphlet cites his advocacy for LGBTQ+ neighbors; no specific policy on gender or reproductive issues cited.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, which amended and narrowed parts of the I-2081 parental-rights list; no campaign statement on the topic.

candidates.summary: Boeing employee and former Mukilteo City Councilmember (2019-2023) running on lower taxes, reduced spending, public safety and parental rights.
highlights: Former Mukilteo City Councilmember and Boeing SPEEA council representative [S1]
Lists 'Lower Taxes' and reducing unnecessary government spending as priorities [S1][S2]
Names protecting parental rights as a priority, without specific proposals [S1][S2]

taxes.basis: Lists lower taxes as a top priority and says Washington's future depends on protecting taxpayers; stated generally, without specific tax proposals.

spending.basis: Supports responsible budgeting and reducing unnecessary government spending, without naming cuts.

experience.basis: One term on a city council and no state office, challenging a twelve-year senator.

parental-rights.basis: Names preserving parental rights as a priority in pamphlet and site, without detail on notification or opt-outs.
